samples.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four square panels side by side, counted from the left. Each panel contains one straight dark fence line drawn all the way across it, and ten small filled dots: some warm coloured (red or orange) and the rest cool coloured (blue), with at least three dots of each colour in every panel. A panel is cleanly fenced when its own fence line has every warm dot of that panel on one side of it and every cool dot of that panel on the other side; which side holds which colour does not matter. Exactly one panel is cleanly fenced; in every other panel at least two dots sit on the wrong side of its fence no matter which way you read it. Every dot centre lies clear of its fence, and every panel holds the same number of dots. The number of warm dots, the number of cool dots, the fence angle, the colours, the amount of ink and the panel position carry no information about the answer: the cleanly fenced panel is not systematically the one with the most warm dots, the steepest fence or the most crowded side. Judge every dot only against the fence drawn in its own panel. Which half of the image contains the cleanly fenced panel, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
